title: The genitive absolute
subtitle: Read a dependent circumstance outside the main clause.
overview: When a participle and its noun are outside the main clause, both may stand in the genitive as a dependent circumstance.
First locate its own genitive subject, then keep it separate from the main clause’s subject and choose its contextual relationship.

sections.title: Construction
rows: when these things had been said

items.en: When the Lord came, they rejoiced.
While the disciples were afraid, he spoke to them.
